lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Alphabet Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Alphabet Garden; TD-001 to TD-010; PA-001 to PA-010; GM-001 to GM-010; AQ-001 to AQ-010.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-001–IL-010, FF-001–FF-010, or FSC-001–FSC-010 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-001–AQ-010; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

demonstrations.setup: Choose 1-3 safe examples of letters and garden words. Keep the group close and materials simple.
demonstrations.demo: Model how to look carefully, then see one example. Use short sentences and point as you speak.
demonstrations.ask: What do you see? Can you show me? How many? What is the same or different?
demonstrations.observe: Look for safe participation, correct pointing/matching/counting and one clear spoken or drawn observation.
demonstrations.check: Learner can show or tell one correct thing without damaging the garden.
demonstrations.close: Repeat the key word, praise careful observation, complete one tiny care action and wash hands.

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize hibiscus, identify its calyx as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the hibiscus? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Alphabet Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Number Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Number Garden; TD-011 to TD-020; PA-011 to PA-020; GM-011 to GM-020; AQ-011 to AQ-020.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-011–IL-020, FF-011–FF-020, or FSC-011–FSC-020 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-011–AQ-020; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize ginger, identify its rhizome as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the ginger? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Number Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.

farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Geometry Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Geometry Garden; TD-021 to TD-030; PA-021 to PA-030; GM-021 to GM-030; AQ-021 to AQ-030.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-021–IL-030, FF-021–FF-030, or FSC-021–FSC-030 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-021–AQ-030; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

demonstrations.setup: Choose 1-3 safe examples of shapes and garden spaces. Keep the group close and materials simple.
demonstrations.demo: Model how to look carefully, then see one example. Use short sentences and point as you speak.
demonstrations.ask: What do you see? Can you show me? How many? What is the same or different?
demonstrations.observe: Look for safe participation, correct pointing/matching/counting and one clear spoken or drawn observation.
demonstrations.check: Learner can show or tell one correct thing without damaging the garden.
demonstrations.close: Repeat the key word, praise careful observation, complete one tiny care action and wash hands.

Draw what you observed and show one important detail.
Find one small garden challenge or difference and tell the teacher what you notice.
Choose one helpful garden action with your teacher and complete it.
Tell one thing you discovered and one thing you want to look for next time.

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize turmeric, identify its rhizome as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the turmeric? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Geometry Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Leaf Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Leaf Garden; TD-031 to TD-040; PA-031 to PA-040; GM-031 to GM-040; AQ-031 to AQ-040.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-031–IL-040, FF-031–FF-040, or FSC-031–FSC-040 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-031–AQ-040; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

demonstrations.setup: Choose 1-3 safe examples of leaf features. Keep the group close and materials simple.
demonstrations.demo: Model how to look carefully, then see one example. Use short sentences and point as you speak.
demonstrations.ask: What do you see? Can you show me? How many? What is the same or different?
demonstrations.observe: Look for safe participation, correct pointing/matching/counting and one clear spoken or drawn observation.
demonstrations.check: Learner can show or tell one correct thing without damaging the garden.
demonstrations.close: Repeat the key word, praise careful observation, complete one tiny care action and wash hands.

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize pineapple, identify its fruit as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the pineapple? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Leaf Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Butterfly Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Butterfly Garden; TD-041 to TD-050; PA-041 to PA-050; GM-041 to GM-050; AQ-041 to AQ-050.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-041–IL-050, FF-041–FF-050, or FSC-041–FSC-050 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-041–AQ-050; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize citrus, identify its fruit as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the citrus? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Butterfly Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the ReBottle Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for ReBottle Garden; TD-051 to TD-060; PA-051 to PA-060; GM-051 to GM-060; AQ-051 to AQ-060.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-051–IL-060, FF-051–FF-060, or FSC-051–FSC-060 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-051–AQ-060; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

demonstrations.setup: Choose 1-3 safe examples of reused bottle planters. Keep the group close and materials simple.
demonstrations.demo: Model how to look carefully, then see one example. Use short sentences and point as you speak.
demonstrations.ask: What do you see? Can you show me? How many? What is the same or different?
demonstrations.observe: Look for safe participation, correct pointing/matching/counting and one clear spoken or drawn observation.
demonstrations.check: Learner can show or tell one correct thing without damaging the garden.
demonstrations.close: Repeat the key word, praise careful observation, complete one tiny care action and wash hands.

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize mint, identify its leaf as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the mint? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the ReBottle Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the MicroGrow Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for MicroGrow Garden; TD-061 to TD-070; PA-061 to PA-070; GM-061 to GM-070; AQ-061 to AQ-070.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-061–IL-070, FF-061–FF-070, or FSC-061–FSC-070 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-061–AQ-070; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

demonstrations.setup: Choose 1-3 safe examples of seedlings. Keep the group close and materials simple.
demonstrations.demo: Model how to look carefully, then see one example. Use short sentences and point as you speak.
demonstrations.ask: What do you see? Can you show me? How many? What is the same or different?
demonstrations.observe: Look for safe participation, correct pointing/matching/counting and one clear spoken or drawn observation.
demonstrations.check: Learner can show or tell one correct thing without damaging the garden.
demonstrations.close: Repeat the key word, praise careful observation, complete one tiny care action and wash hands.

Which action is safest in this garden: A) run, B) look carefully, C) pull plants?
Teacher shows two examples. Which one matches today's garden idea?

Tell one thing you discovered and one thing you want to look for next time.

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize moringa, identify its leaf as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the moringa? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the MicroGrow Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Mini Table Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Mini Table Garden; TD-071 to TD-080; PA-071 to PA-080; GM-071 to GM-080; AQ-071 to AQ-080.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-071–IL-080, FF-071–FF-080, or FSC-071–FSC-080 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-071–AQ-080; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize watermelon, identify its fruit as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the watermelon? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the water/change observation task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the watermelon? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Mini Table Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Sack Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Sack Garden; TD-081 to TD-090; PA-081 to PA-090; GM-081 to GM-090; AQ-081 to AQ-090.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-081–IL-090, FF-081–FF-090, or FSC-081–FSC-090 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-081–AQ-090; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

demonstrations.setup: Choose 1-3 safe examples of sack-grown plants. Keep the group close and materials simple.
demonstrations.demo: Model how to look carefully, then see one example. Use short sentences and point as you speak.
demonstrations.ask: What do you see? Can you show me? How many? What is the same or different?
demonstrations.observe: Look for safe participation, correct pointing/matching/counting and one clear spoken or drawn observation.
demonstrations.check: Learner can show or tell one correct thing without damaging the garden.
demonstrations.close: Repeat the key word, praise careful observation, complete one tiny care action and wash hands.

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize tomato, identify its fruit as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the tomato? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Sack Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Explore the Discovery Garden; name visible features, count or match examples, practise safe garden care and tell one discovery.
lesson.Vocabulary: 5-8 concrete words linked to the week's garden; use picture/word cards, repetition, pointing and oral language.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Discovery Garden; TD-091 to TD-100; PA-091 to PA-100; GM-091 to GM-100; AQ-091 to AQ-100.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-091–IL-100, FF-091–FF-100, or FSC-091–FSC-100 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-091–AQ-100; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Welcome & vocabulary (5-10 min) -> teacher demonstration (5 min) -> supervised garden activity (15-20 min) -> draw/count/tell (10 min) -> care/cleanup (5 min).

demonstrations.setup: Choose 1-3 safe examples of safe garden discoveries. Keep the group close and materials simple.
demonstrations.demo: Model how to look carefully, then see one example. Use short sentences and point as you speak.
demonstrations.ask: What do you see? Can you show me? How many? What is the same or different?
demonstrations.observe: Look for safe participation, correct pointing/matching/counting and one clear spoken or drawn observation.
demonstrations.check: Learner can show or tell one correct thing without damaging the garden.
demonstrations.close: Repeat the key word, praise careful observation, complete one tiny care action and wash hands.

assessments.question: Point to or name one thing in the Discovery Garden that helps you learn about safe garden exploration.
Which action is safest in this garden: A) run, B) look carefully, C) pull plants?
Teacher shows two examples. Which one matches today's garden idea?
Use the observation area to complete a simple task that shows asking and answering simple questions.
Show how to care for or observe the observation area safely.
Count, sort, match or compare something in the Discovery Garden.
Draw what you observed and show one important detail.
Find one small garden challenge or difference and tell the teacher what you notice.
Choose one helpful garden action with your teacher and complete it.
Tell one thing you discovered and one thing you want to look for next time.

ingredientLab.Objective: Help children recognize maize, identify its seed/grain as the food-use plant part, and describe one visible feature.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Teacher shows a clean intact sample or picture. Children look, name, match, sort or draw according to the identity & plant part task. Use only teacher-prepared cut samples for visual observation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Oral naming, pointing/matching, simple sorting, counting or drawing.
ingredientLab.Questions: What do you notice about the maize? Which plant part are we looking at? What colour, shape or texture can you see?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Help children connect the Discovery Garden to the idea of food origin through safe observation, matching, sorting, drawing and talk.
farmToFood.Materials: Picture cards, clean produce examples where approved, baskets/trays, crayons, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Show a garden or food example. 2. Name where it comes from. 3. Let children match, count, sort or draw. 4. Demonstrate clean hands and gentle handling. 5. Ask children to tell one step from garden to food.
farmToFood.Evidence: Correct match, simple count/sort, drawing or oral explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Can the learner show what happens before and after the selected step?
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Alphabet Food Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Alphabet Food Garden; TD-101 to TD-110; PA-101 to PA-110; GM-101 to GM-110; AQ-101 to AQ-110.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-101–IL-110, FF-101–FF-110, or FSC-101–FSC-110 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-101–AQ-110; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

demonstrations.setup: Mark safe work points and prepare simple tools for food-crop vocabulary. Pair pupils where useful.
demonstrations.demo: Show exactly how to observe, including where to start, how to use the tool and how to record the result.
demonstrations.ask: What are we observing or measuring? What did you record? Which result is larger/smaller? Why might they differ?
demonstrations.observe: Check tool handling, units where needed, complete records and whether pupils compare evidence rather than guess.
demonstrations.check: Pupil produces at least two usable observations/measurements and explains one comparison.
demonstrations.close: Share one result, correct a common error, restore tools/site and connect the evidence to the journal or mission card.

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify hibiscus as a calyx, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Use the Alphabet Food Garden to investigate food origin and connect crop production with food people recognize.

farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Observe the crop or production area. 2. Identify the edible plant part or food connection. 3. Complete a safe food origin task. 4. Record a count, measurement, drawing or sequence. 5. Explain the garden-to-food connection.
farmToFood.Evidence: Labeled sequence, tally, measurement, drawing or short explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Scenario: Your group is working with a school garden. You need to use what you learned from the garden to complete a know the ingredient decision.

challenges.Evidence: Short table, sequence, drawing, label comparison, tally or 2-3 sentence explanation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Correct identification; usable evidence; reasonable choice; clear garden-to-food connection.
challenges.Extension: Suggest one way to make the choice reduce waste or protect resources.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Number Food Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Number Food Garden; TD-111 to TD-120; PA-111 to PA-120; GM-111 to GM-120; AQ-111 to AQ-120.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-111–IL-120, FF-111–FF-120, or FSC-111–FSC-120 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-111–AQ-120; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

demonstrations.setup: Mark safe work points and prepare simple tools for counts and simple measurements. Pair pupils where useful.
demonstrations.demo: Show exactly how to observe, including where to start, how to use the tool and how to record the result.
demonstrations.ask: What are we observing or measuring? What did you record? Which result is larger/smaller? Why might they differ?
demonstrations.observe: Check tool handling, units where needed, complete records and whether pupils compare evidence rather than guess.
demonstrations.check: Pupil produces at least two usable observations/measurements and explains one comparison.
demonstrations.close: Share one result, correct a common error, restore tools/site and connect the evidence to the journal or mission card.

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify ginger as a rhizome, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Geometry Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Geometry Garden; TD-121 to TD-130; PA-121 to PA-130; GM-121 to GM-130; AQ-121 to AQ-130.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-121–IL-130, FF-121–FF-130, or FSC-121–FSC-130 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-121–AQ-130; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

demonstrations.setup: Mark safe work points and prepare simple tools for shapes and garden spaces. Pair pupils where useful.
demonstrations.demo: Show exactly how to observe, including where to start, how to use the tool and how to record the result.
demonstrations.ask: What are we observing or measuring? What did you record? Which result is larger/smaller? Why might they differ?
demonstrations.observe: Check tool handling, units where needed, complete records and whether pupils compare evidence rather than guess.
demonstrations.check: Pupil produces at least two usable observations/measurements and explains one comparison.
demonstrations.close: Share one result, correct a common error, restore tools/site and connect the evidence to the journal or mission card.

Make a clear record showing shape or length.
Collect two observations or measurements and compare them.

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify turmeric as a rhizome, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Leaf Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Leaf Garden; TD-131 to TD-140; PA-131 to PA-140; GM-131 to GM-140; AQ-131 to AQ-140.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-131–IL-140, FF-131–FF-140, or FSC-131–FSC-140 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-131–AQ-140; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify pineapple as a fruit, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Use the Leaf Garden to investigate food origin and connect crop production with food people recognize.
farmToFood.Materials: Student journal, crop/food picture cards, clean trays, ruler or scale where available, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Observe the crop or production area. 2. Identify the edible plant part or food connection. 3. Complete a safe food origin task. 4. Record a count, measurement, drawing or sequence. 5. Explain the garden-to-food connection.
farmToFood.Evidence: Labeled sequence, tally, measurement, drawing or short explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Scenario: Your group is working with a ingredient display. You need to use what you learned from the garden to complete a know the ingredient decision.
challenges.Task: Identify the important information, compare at least two options, choose an action and explain your choice with one observation or measurement.
challenges.Evidence: Short table, sequence, drawing, label comparison, tally or 2-3 sentence explanation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Correct identification; usable evidence; reasonable choice; clear garden-to-food connection.
challenges.Extension: Suggest one way to make the choice reduce waste or protect resources.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Pollinator Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Pollinator Garden; TD-141 to TD-150; PA-141 to PA-150; GM-141 to GM-150; AQ-141 to AQ-150.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-141–IL-150, FF-141–FF-150, or FSC-141–FSC-150 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-141–AQ-150; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify citrus as a fruit, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Use the Pollinator Garden to investigate food origin and connect crop production with food people recognize.
farmToFood.Materials: Student journal, crop/food picture cards, clean trays, ruler or scale where available, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Observe the crop or production area. 2. Identify the edible plant part or food connection. 3. Complete a safe food origin task. 4. Record a count, measurement, drawing or sequence. 5. Explain the garden-to-food connection.
farmToFood.Evidence: Labeled sequence, tally, measurement, drawing or short explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Raised Food Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Raised Food Garden; TD-151 to TD-160; PA-151 to PA-160; GM-151 to GM-160; AQ-151 to AQ-160.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-151–IL-160, FF-151–FF-160, or FSC-151–FSC-160 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-151–AQ-160; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

demonstrations.setup: Mark safe work points and prepare simple tools for raised-bed growth and spacing. Pair pupils where useful.
demonstrations.demo: Show exactly how to observe, including where to start, how to use the tool and how to record the result.
demonstrations.ask: What are we observing or measuring? What did you record? Which result is larger/smaller? Why might they differ?
demonstrations.observe: Check tool handling, units where needed, complete records and whether pupils compare evidence rather than guess.
demonstrations.check: Pupil produces at least two usable observations/measurements and explains one comparison.
demonstrations.close: Share one result, correct a common error, restore tools/site and connect the evidence to the journal or mission card.

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify mint as a leaf, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Use the Raised Food Garden to investigate food origin and connect crop production with food people recognize.
farmToFood.Materials: Student journal, crop/food picture cards, clean trays, ruler or scale where available, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Observe the crop or production area. 2. Identify the edible plant part or food connection. 3. Complete a safe food origin task. 4. Record a count, measurement, drawing or sequence. 5. Explain the garden-to-food connection.
farmToFood.Evidence: Labeled sequence, tally, measurement, drawing or short explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

farmToFood.Steps: 1. Observe the crop or production area. 2. Identify the edible plant part or food connection. 3. Complete a safe waste-to-resource task. 4. Record a count, measurement, drawing or sequence. 5. Explain the garden-to-food connection.
farmToFood.Evidence: Labeled sequence, tally, measurement, drawing or short explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Scenario: Your group is working with a water station. You need to use what you learned from the garden to complete a know the ingredient decision.
challenges.Task: Identify the important information, compare at least two options, choose an action and explain your choice with one observation or measurement.
challenges.Evidence: Short table, sequence, drawing, label comparison, tally or 2-3 sentence explanation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Correct identification; usable evidence; reasonable choice; clear garden-to-food connection.
challenges.Extension: Suggest one way to make the choice reduce waste or protect resources.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the ReBottle Wall Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for ReBottle Wall Garden; TD-161 to TD-170; PA-161 to PA-170; GM-161 to GM-170; AQ-161 to AQ-170.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-161–IL-170, FF-161–FF-170, or FSC-161–FSC-170 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-161–AQ-170; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify moringa as a leaf, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Use the ReBottle Wall Garden to investigate food origin and connect crop production with food people recognize.

farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Sack GrowBag Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Sack GrowBag Garden; TD-171 to TD-180; PA-171 to PA-180; GM-171 to GM-180; AQ-171 to AQ-180.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-171–IL-180, FF-171–FF-180, or FSC-171–FSC-180 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-171–AQ-180; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify watermelon as a fruit, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Use the Sack GrowBag Garden to investigate food origin and connect crop production with food people recognize.
farmToFood.Materials: Student journal, crop/food picture cards, clean trays, ruler or scale where available, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Observe the crop or production area. 2. Identify the edible plant part or food connection. 3. Complete a safe food origin task. 4. Record a count, measurement, drawing or sequence. 5. Explain the garden-to-food connection.
farmToFood.Evidence: Labeled sequence, tally, measurement, drawing or short explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Ground Production Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Ground Production Garden; TD-181 to TD-190; PA-181 to PA-190; GM-181 to GM-190; AQ-181 to AQ-190.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-181–IL-190, FF-181–FF-190, or FSC-181–FSC-190 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-181–AQ-190; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

demonstrations.setup: Mark safe work points and prepare simple tools for rows, spacing and stand. Pair pupils where useful.
demonstrations.demo: Show exactly how to observe, including where to start, how to use the tool and how to record the result.
demonstrations.ask: What are we observing or measuring? What did you record? Which result is larger/smaller? Why might they differ?
demonstrations.observe: Check tool handling, units where needed, complete records and whether pupils compare evidence rather than guess.
demonstrations.check: Pupil produces at least two usable observations/measurements and explains one comparison.
demonstrations.close: Share one result, correct a common error, restore tools/site and connect the evidence to the journal or mission card.

missions.success: My record is complete, my numbers or observations are clear, and my explanation uses evidence.
missions.safety: Stay on paths where provided. Follow teacher instructions and school garden safety rules.
missions.agrishine: Identify one small, safe improvement or care action for the Ground Production Garden and explain why it may help.

assessments.question: What is one important idea in row length, plant spacing and stand establishment?
Which tool or method could help you study the crop row?
Why should measurements or counts be written down?
assessments.answer: So evidence can be checked, compared and remembered.

assessments.question: Demonstrate how to observe or measure the crop row safely.
Make a clear record showing row record.

Make a tally, table, picture graph or labeled drawing from your evidence.
A classmate gets a different result. Give one reasonable reason the results may differ.
assessments.answer: Accept sampling, position, timing, method or natural variation.

assessments.question: Recommend one safe garden-care improvement using your evidence.
Write one new question that could be tested in the Ground Production Garden.
assessments.answer: Question must be observable/measurable and safe.

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify tomato as a fruit, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Use the Ground Production Garden to investigate food origin and connect crop production with food people recognize.
farmToFood.Materials: Student journal, crop/food picture cards, clean trays, ruler or scale where available, labels, handwashing supplies.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Observe the crop or production area. 2. Identify the edible plant part or food connection. 3. Complete a safe food origin task. 4. Record a count, measurement, drawing or sequence. 5. Explain the garden-to-food connection.
farmToFood.Evidence: Labeled sequence, tally, measurement, drawing or short explanation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Identify one action that protects food quality or reduces waste.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Observe the Discovery Production Garden, make a simple measurement or comparison, record evidence and explain one finding.
lesson.Vocabulary: 8-12 garden and measurement words; require learners to use selected terms in their journal.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Discovery Production Garden; TD-191 to TD-200; PA-191 to PA-200; GM-191 to GM-200; AQ-191 to AQ-200.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-191–IL-200, FF-191–FF-200, or FSC-191–FSC-200 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-191–AQ-200; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/vocabulary (10 min) -> demonstration (10 min) -> practical investigation (25 min) -> journal record (15 min) -> mission/reflection (10 min).

demonstrations.setup: Mark safe work points and prepare simple tools for measurable production questions. Pair pupils where useful.
demonstrations.demo: Show exactly how to observe, including where to start, how to use the tool and how to record the result.
demonstrations.ask: What are we observing or measuring? What did you record? Which result is larger/smaller? Why might they differ?
demonstrations.observe: Check tool handling, units where needed, complete records and whether pupils compare evidence rather than guess.
demonstrations.check: Pupil produces at least two usable observations/measurements and explains one comparison.
demonstrations.close: Share one result, correct a common error, restore tools/site and connect the evidence to the journal or mission card.

assessments.question: What is one important idea in student-led garden questions?
Which tool or method could help you study the production plot?
Why should measurements or counts be written down?
assessments.answer: So evidence can be checked, compared and remembered.

assessments.question: Demonstrate how to observe or measure the production plot safely.
Make a clear record showing investigation record.
Collect two observations or measurements and compare them.
Make a tally, table, picture graph or labeled drawing from your evidence.
A classmate gets a different result. Give one reasonable reason the results may differ.
assessments.answer: Accept sampling, position, timing, method or natural variation.

assessments.question: Recommend one safe garden-care improvement using your evidence.
Write one new question that could be tested in the Discovery Production Garden.
assessments.answer: Question must be observable/measurable and safe.

ingredientLab.Objective: Observe and classify maize as a seed/grain, then use simple measurement or comparison to investigate identity & plant part.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Observe teacher-approved samples, record visible properties, make a count or simple measurement, compare two examples, and write/draw the result.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Labeled observation, simple table, measurement, comparison sentence or diagram.
ingredientLab.Questions: What did you observe? Which property can we measure? How are the samples similar or different?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Frame and investigate a measurable question in the Raised Food Garden, analyze evidence and explain a limitation.
lesson.Vocabulary: 10-15 scientific terms linked to variables, measurement, data, garden processes and evidence.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Raised Food Garden; TD-201 to TD-210; PA-201 to PA-210; GM-201 to GM-210; AQ-201 to AQ-210.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-201–IL-210, FF-201–FF-210, or FSC-201–FSC-210 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-201–AQ-210; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Investigation question (10 min) -> method/safety demonstration (10 min) -> sampling/data collection (30 min) -> calculation/graph (15 min) -> conclusion/mission (10 min).

assessments.question: Define or explain one core idea related to raised-bed crop growth and spacing.
Why is a fair comparison important when studying the raised bed?
assessments.answer: It reduces bias and supports a valid comparison.

assessments.question: What should be kept the same when comparing two conditions?
Use an appropriate tool to collect a repeatable measurement.
Show one quality or safety check before recording the result.
Collect at least three values and calculate a useful summary such as mean, range, rate or percentage.
Graph or tabulate the result and identify the main pattern.
Identify one limitation in your investigation and explain how it could affect the result.
Recommend one management or design change based on the evidence.
Design a follow-up test that would strengthen the conclusion.
assessments.answer: Testable, safe follow-up with clear variable/metric.

ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Frame a question, select comparable samples, measure the relevant property, repeat observations, summarize the data and explain the pattern and one limitation.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Question, sample IDs, data table, calculation/graph, conclusion and limitation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Is the comparison fair? What variable are you measuring? What pattern is supported by the data?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.
