lesson.Learning_Objective: Conduct a structured investigation in the Soilless Learning Garden, quantify a response and convert evidence into a management recommendation.
lesson.Vocabulary: 12-18 scientific and systems terms; students must use terminology precisely in method, results and recommendation.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Soilless Learning Garden; TD-371 to TD-380; PA-371 to PA-380; GM-371 to GM-380; AQ-371 to AQ-380.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-371–IL-380, FF-371–FF-380, or FSC-371–FSC-380 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-371–AQ-380; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/hypothesis (10 min) -> protocol/QC (15 min) -> replicated data collection (35 min) -> analysis (20 min) -> management decision (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Test a hypothesis about identity & plant part in watermelon, quantify variation or change, and evaluate implications for ingredient quality or handling.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define hypothesis and variables; label replicates; collect traceable measurements; calculate a summary/effect; graph where useful; identify uncertainty; recommend a handling or quality decision.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Hypothesis, protocol, replicate data, quantitative analysis, graph, uncertainty and recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: What is the response variable? How much variation is present? Does the evidence support the hypothesis? What decision follows?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Conduct a structured investigation in the Sensor-Ready Garden, quantify a response and convert evidence into a management recommendation.
lesson.Vocabulary: 12-18 scientific and systems terms; students must use terminology precisely in method, results and recommendation.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Sensor-Ready Garden; TD-381 to TD-390; PA-381 to PA-390; GM-381 to GM-390; AQ-381 to AQ-390.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-381–IL-390, FF-381–FF-390, or FSC-381–FSC-390 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-381–AQ-390; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/hypothesis (10 min) -> protocol/QC (15 min) -> replicated data collection (35 min) -> analysis (20 min) -> management decision (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Test a hypothesis about identity & plant part in tomato, quantify variation or change, and evaluate implications for ingredient quality or handling.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define hypothesis and variables; label replicates; collect traceable measurements; calculate a summary/effect; graph where useful; identify uncertainty; recommend a handling or quality decision.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Hypothesis, protocol, replicate data, quantitative analysis, graph, uncertainty and recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: What is the response variable? How much variation is present? Does the evidence support the hypothesis? What decision follows?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define hypothesis and variables; label replicates; collect traceable measurements; calculate a summary/effect; graph where useful; identify uncertainty; recommend a handling or quality decision.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Hypothesis, protocol, replicate data, quantitative analysis, graph, uncertainty and recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: What is the response variable? How much variation is present? Does the evidence support the hypothesis? What decision follows?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Analyze food origin as a production and post-harvest problem in the Sensor-Ready Garden, quantify relevant evidence and justify a management decision.
farmToFood.Materials: Investigation journal, sample IDs, balance/measurement tools where available, clean containers, quality checklist, calculator.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define the farm-to-food problem. 2. Establish sample and quality criteria. 3. Collect traceable data. 4. Quantify yield, quality class, loss or process performance as appropriate. 5. Identify a critical loss/handling point. 6. Recommend a management response.
farmToFood.Evidence: Traceable dataset, quality/loss calculation, process map and qualified recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Define a measurable threshold that would trigger the recommended action.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Scenario: The school is reviewing a food journey map. You are assigned a know the ingredient problem that requires a defensible management decision.
challenges.Task: Define criteria and variables, collect or interpret traceable data, quantify the relevant difference/loss/use, evaluate uncertainty and recommend an action with a trigger or threshold.
challenges.Evidence: Problem statement, data/calculation, evaluation, uncertainty note and management recommendation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Traceable evidence; quantitative reasoning; explicit criteria; qualified conclusion; actionable recommendation.
challenges.Extension: Conduct a sensitivity check: identify one assumption that could reverse the decision.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Conduct a structured investigation in the Applied Systems Garden, quantify a response and convert evidence into a management recommendation.
lesson.Vocabulary: 12-18 scientific and systems terms; students must use terminology precisely in method, results and recommendation.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Applied Systems Garden; TD-391 to TD-400; PA-391 to PA-400; GM-391 to GM-400; AQ-391 to AQ-400.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-391–IL-400, FF-391–FF-400, or FSC-391–FSC-400 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-391–AQ-400; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Question/hypothesis (10 min) -> protocol/QC (15 min) -> replicated data collection (35 min) -> analysis (20 min) -> management decision (10 min).

demonstrations.setup: Prepare hypothesis, variables, treatment/comparison, replicates and QC for stocks, flows, feedbacks and trade-offs. Assign sample/instrument IDs.
demonstrations.demo: Demonstrate how to question according to protocol, including raw-data recording and one quality-control check.
demonstrations.ask: What is the hypothesis? Which variable is the response? Why replicate? What is the effect? What uncertainty qualifies the conclusion?
demonstrations.observe: Check protocol fidelity, traceable raw data, units, replicate handling, analysis and scientific integrity.
demonstrations.check: Student quantifies the response, identifies variation/uncertainty and makes a qualified conclusion or management recommendation.
demonstrations.close: Review abnormal readings without deleting them, connect evidence to management, secure instruments and record follow-up.

ingredientLab.Objective: Test a hypothesis about identity & plant part in maize, quantify variation or change, and evaluate implications for ingredient quality or handling.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define hypothesis and variables; label replicates; collect traceable measurements; calculate a summary/effect; graph where useful; identify uncertainty; recommend a handling or quality decision.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Hypothesis, protocol, replicate data, quantitative analysis, graph, uncertainty and recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: What is the response variable? How much variation is present? Does the evidence support the hypothesis? What decision follows?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Analyze food origin as a production and post-harvest problem in the Applied Systems Garden, quantify relevant evidence and justify a management decision.
farmToFood.Materials: Investigation journal, sample IDs, balance/measurement tools where available, clean containers, quality checklist, calculator.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define the farm-to-food problem. 2. Establish sample and quality criteria. 3. Collect traceable data. 4. Quantify yield, quality class, loss or process performance as appropriate. 5. Identify a critical loss/handling point. 6. Recommend a management response.
farmToFood.Evidence: Traceable dataset, quality/loss calculation, process map and qualified recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Define a measurable threshold that would trigger the recommended action.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Advanced Production Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Advanced Production Garden; TD-401 to TD-410; PA-401 to PA-410; GM-401 to GM-410; AQ-401 to AQ-410.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-401–IL-410, FF-401–FF-410, or FSC-401–FSC-410 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-401–AQ-410; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in hibiscus, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Scenario: A school food-system design team is evaluating a school garden. Your role is to frame and solve a know the ingredient challenge under performance, resource and safety constraints.
challenges.Task: Define system boundary, objective and constraints; establish indicators; compare scenarios; quantify a performance metric; identify trade-offs and uncertainty; recommend an optimized or robust option with acceptance criteria.
challenges.Evidence: System/process map, metric or model, scenario comparison, uncertainty/trade-off analysis and recommendation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Clear objective; valid indicators; reproducible reasoning; constraints respected; recommendation tied to measurable acceptance criteria.
challenges.Extension: Design a pilot test, monitoring plan or decision rule to validate the recommendation.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Crop Trial Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Crop Trial Garden; TD-411 to TD-420; PA-411 to PA-420; GM-411 to GM-420; AQ-411 to AQ-420.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-411–IL-420, FF-411–FF-420, or FSC-411–FSC-420 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-411–AQ-420; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

assessments.question: Frame a research or engineering question involving replicated treatments, blocks, variability and treatment effects.
assessments.answer: Precise question with system boundary and measurable performance outcome.

assessments.question: Identify one assumption and one constraint relevant to the crop trial.
Explain why validation is distinct from calibration or fitting.
assessments.answer: Validation tests performance on independent/held-out evidence; calibration/fitting sets model/instrument relation.

assessments.question: Execute or demonstrate a technically appropriate measurement of treatment effect, with instrument ID, unit and QC note.
Document one calibration, verification or reference check.
Analyze a dataset using an appropriate quantitative metric and state uncertainty.
assessments.answer: Correct metric, units and uncertainty statement.

assessments.question: Compare at least two scenarios/designs and quantify the performance trade-off.
Stress-test the conclusion by changing one assumption or input and report whether the decision changes.
Recommend an optimization and define a measurable acceptance criterion.
Write a decision statement integrating performance, uncertainty, safety and implementation constraints.

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in ginger, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Controlled Experiment Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Controlled Experiment Garden; TD-421 to TD-430; PA-421 to PA-430; GM-421 to GM-430; AQ-421 to AQ-430.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-421–IL-430, FF-421–FF-430, or FSC-421–FSC-430 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-421–AQ-430; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

assessments.question: Frame a research or engineering question involving causal variables, factorial effects, confounding and sensitivity.
assessments.answer: Precise question with system boundary and measurable performance outcome.

assessments.question: Identify one assumption and one constraint relevant to the controlled experiment.
Explain why validation is distinct from calibration or fitting.
assessments.answer: Validation tests performance on independent/held-out evidence; calibration/fitting sets model/instrument relation.

assessments.question: Execute or demonstrate a technically appropriate measurement of experimental metric, with instrument ID, unit and QC note.
Document one calibration, verification or reference check.
Analyze a dataset using an appropriate quantitative metric and state uncertainty.
assessments.answer: Correct metric, units and uncertainty statement.

assessments.question: Compare at least two scenarios/designs and quantify the performance trade-off.
Stress-test the conclusion by changing one assumption or input and report whether the decision changes.
Recommend an optimization and define a measurable acceptance criterion.
Write a decision statement integrating performance, uncertainty, safety and implementation constraints.

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in turmeric, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Evaluate food origin as part of the Controlled Experiment Garden food-system chain, integrating production, quality, process efficiency, safety constraints and design decisions.
farmToFood.Materials: Research journal, system/process map, measurement instruments, quality records, calculator/computer where available, clean handling materials.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define system boundary and performance objective. 2. Map the product/material flow. 3. Quantify a production, quality, loss, storage or process metric. 4. Identify bottleneck and uncertainty. 5. Compare two management/design scenarios. 6. Recommend an optimization with acceptance criteria.
farmToFood.Evidence: Process-flow diagram, quantitative metric, scenario comparison, uncertainty note and defensible recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Propose a next-stage test or prototype that improves farm-to-food performance without weakening safety.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Success_Criteria: Clear objective; valid indicators; reproducible reasoning; constraints respected; recommendation tied to measurable acceptance criteria.
challenges.Extension: Design a pilot test, monitoring plan or decision rule to validate the recommendation.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Irrigation Engineering Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Irrigation Engineering Garden; TD-431 to TD-440; PA-431 to PA-440; GM-431 to GM-440; AQ-431 to AQ-440.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-431–IL-440, FF-431–FF-440, or FSC-431–FSC-440 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-431–AQ-440; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in pineapple, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Evaluate food origin as part of the Irrigation Engineering Garden food-system chain, integrating production, quality, process efficiency, safety constraints and design decisions.
farmToFood.Materials: Research journal, system/process map, measurement instruments, quality records, calculator/computer where available, clean handling materials.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define system boundary and performance objective. 2. Map the product/material flow. 3. Quantify a production, quality, loss, storage or process metric. 4. Identify bottleneck and uncertainty. 5. Compare two management/design scenarios. 6. Recommend an optimization with acceptance criteria.
farmToFood.Evidence: Process-flow diagram, quantitative metric, scenario comparison, uncertainty note and defensible recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Propose a next-stage test or prototype that improves farm-to-food performance without weakening safety.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Water Productivity Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Water Productivity Garden; TD-441 to TD-450; PA-441 to PA-450; GM-441 to GM-450; AQ-441 to AQ-450.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-441–IL-450, FF-441–FF-450, or FSC-441–FSC-450 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-441–AQ-450; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

assessments.question: Frame a research or engineering question involving water balance, ET, IWP and ET water productivity.
assessments.answer: Precise question with system boundary and measurable performance outcome.

assessments.question: Identify one assumption and one constraint relevant to the water-productivity dataset.
Explain why validation is distinct from calibration or fitting.
assessments.answer: Validation tests performance on independent/held-out evidence; calibration/fitting sets model/instrument relation.

assessments.question: Execute or demonstrate a technically appropriate measurement of water-productivity metric, with instrument ID, unit and QC note.
Document one calibration, verification or reference check.
Analyze a dataset using an appropriate quantitative metric and state uncertainty.
assessments.answer: Correct metric, units and uncertainty statement.

assessments.question: Compare at least two scenarios/designs and quantify the performance trade-off.
Stress-test the conclusion by changing one assumption or input and report whether the decision changes.
Recommend an optimization and define a measurable acceptance criterion.
Write a decision statement integrating performance, uncertainty, safety and implementation constraints.

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in citrus, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Evaluate food origin as part of the Water Productivity Garden food-system chain, integrating production, quality, process efficiency, safety constraints and design decisions.
farmToFood.Materials: Research journal, system/process map, measurement instruments, quality records, calculator/computer where available, clean handling materials.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define system boundary and performance objective. 2. Map the product/material flow. 3. Quantify a production, quality, loss, storage or process metric. 4. Identify bottleneck and uncertainty. 5. Compare two management/design scenarios. 6. Recommend an optimization with acceptance criteria.
farmToFood.Evidence: Process-flow diagram, quantitative metric, scenario comparison, uncertainty note and defensible recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Propose a next-stage test or prototype that improves farm-to-food performance without weakening safety.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Scenario: A school food-system design team is evaluating a school lunch scenario. Your role is to frame and solve a know the ingredient challenge under performance, resource and safety constraints.
challenges.Task: Define system boundary, objective and constraints; establish indicators; compare scenarios; quantify a performance metric; identify trade-offs and uncertainty; recommend an optimized or robust option with acceptance criteria.
challenges.Evidence: System/process map, metric or model, scenario comparison, uncertainty/trade-off analysis and recommendation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Clear objective; valid indicators; reproducible reasoning; constraints respected; recommendation tied to measurable acceptance criteria.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Advanced Soilless Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Advanced Soilless Garden; TD-451 to TD-460; PA-451 to PA-460; GM-451 to GM-460; AQ-451 to AQ-460.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-451–IL-460, FF-451–FF-460, or FSC-451–FSC-460 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-451–AQ-460; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

missions.title: FRAME FOR PERFORMANCE
missions.mission: Frame and execute a research or engineering mission on recirculating soilless control. Produce quantitative evidence that can support a design or management decision.
missions.materials: pH/EC meters, flow data, system map
missions.evidence: pH/EC dynamics, residence time or diagnostic evidence
missions.success: The method is reproducible, assumptions are explicit, uncertainty is addressed, and the recommendation is technically defensible.
missions.safety: Teacher supervises nutrient-solution work. Follow teacher instructions and school garden safety rules.
missions.agrishine: Propose one optimization or next-stage prototype/test for the Advanced Soilless Garden, including a measurable acceptance criterion.

challenges.Success_Criteria: Clear objective; valid indicators; reproducible reasoning; constraints respected; recommendation tied to measurable acceptance criteria.
challenges.Extension: Design a pilot test, monitoring plan or decision rule to validate the recommendation.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Sensor & Monitoring Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Sensor & Monitoring Garden; TD-461 to TD-470; PA-461 to PA-470; GM-461 to GM-470; AQ-461 to AQ-470.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-461–IL-470, FF-461–FF-470, or FSC-461–FSC-470 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-461–AQ-470; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in moringa, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?

farmToFood.Objective: Evaluate food origin as part of the Sensor & Monitoring Garden food-system chain, integrating production, quality, process efficiency, safety constraints and design decisions.

farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define system boundary and performance objective. 2. Map the product/material flow. 3. Quantify a production, quality, loss, storage or process metric. 4. farmToFood.Evidence: Process-flow diagram, quantitative metric, scenario comparison, uncertainty note and defensible recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Propose a next-stage test or prototype that improves farm-to-food performance without weakening safety.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

passport.verification: Teacher verifies when evidence is sufficient and safe practice is demonstrated.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Smart Irrigation Demonstrator, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Smart Irrigation Demonstrator; TD-471 to TD-480; PA-471 to PA-480; GM-471 to GM-480; AQ-471 to AQ-480.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-471–IL-480, FF-471–FF-480, or FSC-471–FSC-480 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-471–AQ-480; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in watermelon, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Research & Design Garden, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Research & Design Garden; TD-481 to TD-490; PA-481 to PA-490; GM-481 to GM-490; AQ-481 to AQ-490.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-481–IL-490, FF-481–FF-490, or FSC-481–FSC-490 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-481–AQ-490; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

assessments.question: Compare at least two scenarios/designs and quantify the performance trade-off.
Stress-test the conclusion by changing one assumption or input and report whether the decision changes.
Recommend an optimization and define a measurable acceptance criterion.
Write a decision statement integrating performance, uncertainty, safety and implementation constraints.

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in tomato, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Evaluate food origin as part of the Research & Design Garden food-system chain, integrating production, quality, process efficiency, safety constraints and design decisions.
farmToFood.Materials: Research journal, system/process map, measurement instruments, quality records, calculator/computer where available, clean handling materials.

challenges.Scenario: A school food-system design team is evaluating a food journey map. Your role is to frame and solve a know the ingredient challenge under performance, resource and safety constraints.
challenges.Task: Define system boundary, objective and constraints; establish indicators; compare scenarios; quantify a performance metric; identify trade-offs and uncertainty; recommend an optimized or robust option with acceptance criteria.
challenges.Evidence: System/process map, metric or model, scenario comparison, uncertainty/trade-off analysis and recommendation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Clear objective; valid indicators; reproducible reasoning; constraints respected; recommendation tied to measurable acceptance criteria.
challenges.Extension: Design a pilot test, monitoring plan or decision rule to validate the recommendation.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.

lesson.Learning_Objective: Design and evaluate a research/engineering investigation in the Integrated Food Systems Laboratory, including measurement quality, uncertainty and an optimization decision.
lesson.Vocabulary: 15-20 research, engineering, instrumentation, modeling and systems terms used in technical context.
lesson.Resource_Links: Flashcards for Integrated Food Systems Laboratory; TD-491 to TD-500; PA-491 to PA-500; GM-491 to GM-500; AQ-491 to AQ-500.
lesson.Integrated_Extension: Select one IL-491–IL-500, FF-491–FF-500, or FSC-491–FSC-500 activity where it fits the week's garden evidence.
lesson.Assessment: Use observation plus AQ-491–AQ-500; record practical, data/investigation and mission problem-solving evidence in the Food Smart Passport.
lesson.Suggested_Flow: Research/design objective (10 min) -> protocol/instrument/QC (20 min) -> data/model work (40 min) -> validation/trade-off analysis (20 min) -> optimization recommendation (10 min).

Explain why validation is distinct from calibration or fitting.

assessments.question: Execute or demonstrate a technically appropriate measurement of integrated-system metric, with instrument ID, unit and QC note.
Document one calibration, verification or reference check.
Analyze a dataset using an appropriate quantitative metric and state uncertainty.
assessments.answer: Correct metric, units and uncertainty statement.

assessments.question: Compare at least two scenarios/designs and quantify the performance trade-off.
Stress-test the conclusion by changing one assumption or input and report whether the decision changes.
Recommend an optimization and define a measurable acceptance criterion.
Write a decision statement integrating performance, uncertainty, safety and implementation constraints.

ingredientLab.Objective: Design a research or product-development investigation of identity & plant part in maize, integrating measurement quality, process flow, validation and optimization.
ingredientLab.Materials: Clean ingredient samples or images, labels, observation sheet/journal, ruler and balance where appropriate, clean trays/containers, handwashing supplies.
ingredientLab.DIY: Use locally available produce, paper labels, clean food-grade reused containers, handmade measuring grids and simple classroom balances where suitable.
ingredientLab.Method: Define performance objective and acceptance criteria; specify sample/process boundary; establish measurement/QC protocol; collect and model data; validate against reference evidence; compare scenarios; recommend optimization.
ingredientLab.Evidence: Protocol, traceable dataset, QC/validation record, model or quantitative comparison, uncertainty and optimization recommendation.
ingredientLab.Questions: Which decision must the evidence support? How is measurement quality verified? What trade-off constrains the preferred process or specification?
ingredientLab.Safety: No tasting is required. Use clean teacher-approved samples. Wash hands before and after handling. Teachers alone control knives, graters, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery. Do not conduct microbial culture or unsafe food-storage experiments.

farmToFood.Objective: Evaluate food origin as part of the Integrated Food Systems Laboratory food-system chain, integrating production, quality, process efficiency, safety constraints and design decisions.
farmToFood.Materials: Research journal, system/process map, measurement instruments, quality records, calculator/computer where available, clean handling materials.
farmToFood.DIY: Use locally available baskets, clean reused food-grade containers, handmade labels, paper process cards and simple balances/measuring vessels where suitable.
farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define system boundary and performance objective. 2. Map the product/material flow. 3. Quantify a production, quality, loss, storage or process metric. 4. Identify bottleneck and uncertainty. 5. Compare two management/design scenarios. 6. Recommend an optimization with acceptance criteria.
farmToFood.Evidence: Process-flow diagram, quantitative metric, scenario comparison, uncertainty note and defensible recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Propose a next-stage test or prototype that improves farm-to-food performance without weakening safety.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

farmToFood.Steps: 1. Define system boundary and performance objective. 2. Map the product/material flow. 3. Quantify a production, quality, loss, storage or process metric. 4. Identify bottleneck and uncertainty. 5. Compare two management/design scenarios. 6. Recommend an optimization with acceptance criteria.
farmToFood.Evidence: Process-flow diagram, quantitative metric, scenario comparison, uncertainty note and defensible recommendation.
farmToFood.Challenge: Propose a next-stage test or prototype that improves farm-to-food performance without weakening safety.
farmToFood.Safety: No tasting unless the school has separately approved a supervised food activity. Wash hands before and after handling produce. Use only clean, teacher-approved samples and containers. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and any processing machinery.

challenges.Scenario: A school food-system design team is evaluating a school food-waste station. Your role is to frame and solve a know the ingredient challenge under performance, resource and safety constraints.
challenges.Task: Define system boundary, objective and constraints; establish indicators; compare scenarios; quantify a performance metric; identify trade-offs and uncertainty; recommend an optimized or robust option with acceptance criteria.
challenges.Evidence: System/process map, metric or model, scenario comparison, uncertainty/trade-off analysis and recommendation.
challenges.Success_Criteria: Clear objective; valid indicators; reproducible reasoning; constraints respected; recommendation tied to measurable acceptance criteria.
challenges.Extension: Design a pilot test, monitoring plan or decision rule to validate the recommendation.
challenges.Safety: Use only teacher-approved materials. No tasting is required. Follow school rules for food handling, allergies, handwashing and sanitation. Teachers control knives, heat, electrical equipment, chemicals and processing machinery.
